interpretation.build_flags: Native binary is the same 5081… build across arms; Veortex V45.1 is the same 90d54… build where selected. Official native compiler flags are not matched to Veortex.
interpretation.client_change: Historical client SHA 9dab9e7f2292d6b3ccae108335317b2f249cf0e83a7cada02650060c91b9c251; current client SHA is recorded per row (5477653066b11acf0ce1f53545f6bd98aad9175ed3c4072a89b051298e05cde0 in the live campaign). The Go main change is limited to the B128 allowlist/help text.
interpretation.comparison_type: Overall CPU policy comparison; not a pure cores-scaling experiment.
interpretation.cpu_measurement: Historical CPU observers establish role/affinity activity but do not provide a whole-process aggregate. Current rows provide whole-process CPU equivalents per node; no historical process utilization is inferred.
interpretation.current_budget: Both containers use three vCPUs per node shared by all server phases. Native MAX_SEARCH_THREADS=3; Veortex max ring workers=3 and Rayon=3; separate TopK disabled; no per-thread affinity. Current phase permissions use the full three-CPU mask symmetrically.
interpretation.historical_budget: Both containers always had three vCPUs per node. Native full search was pinned to one search CPU with two support CPUs. Veortex scan was pinned to one scan CPU, while TopK, FP32 reranking, and payload work could use the two support CPUs. Old phase permissions were asymmetric across engines.
interpretation.older_cross_engine_claims: Older 40–50x cross-engine throughput claims are not a compute-equivalent baseline because search/scan and support-phase CPU permissions differed. The matched-resource three-CPU RPS ratios here supersede those figures for full-budget throughput claims.
interpretation.quality: Every included row must be accepted, have zero timed errors, match every returned ordered Top10 against exact FP32 truth, and pass all 1,024 initial category checks. This is empirical corpus coverage, not a universal recall guarantee.
interpretation.query_and_manifest: Pinned query corpus SHA-256 begins 90c486 and is the same. Manifest SHA values can differ because the comparison label differs; this does not imply different query content.
interpretation.scaling_clarification: The old total CPU budget was three vCPUs per node, not one. A 2.8–2.9x scan-only throughput target requires three busy scan workers and sufficient shared CPU/memory capacity. This campaign did not isolate 1-vs-3-worker scan throughput; it reports end-to-end performance and current whole-process CPU equivalents.
interpretation.timing_order: Measurements occurred at different times and used fixed run orders; no randomized ABBA replication.
